item.title: Student Engagement Specialist School Of Public Policy
item.description: APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS: CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process . Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday. CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday. Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants . This position is funded for 1 year(s); continuation past 1 year(s) will be based on university need, performance, and/or availability of funding. ​ POSITION SPECIFICS ​ The School of Public Policy is seeking a Student Engagement Specialist to lead student engagement initiatives and support student success through community-building, programming, leadership development, career readiness, and student-focused events. The School of Public Policy (SPP) seeks to develop professionals who have the skills to identify, analyze, and solve our major policy issues. Professional development opportunities extend beyond the classroom to career days in Washington, D.C., and Harrisburg, Pennsylvania; the Local Government Expo; policy simulations; and the Next Gen Leadership Academy. The Student Engagement Specialist is at the heart of academic operations for the School’s graduate and undergraduate programs, with experiential learning opportunities, community engagement, and career exploration enhancing student success and career readiness. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Develop and facilitate the School’s Harrisburg and Washington, D.C., career exploration trips Develop and facilitate Next Gen Leadership Academy programming Provide support for the School’s Local Government Initiative Build and maintain relationships with external stakeholders, alumni, and friends of the School Develop and facilitate the School’s fall and spring policy simulation events Participate in SPP leadership meetings, committee meetings, and faculty meetings Attend SPP student and public engagement events Participate in Board of Visitors meetings to discuss student engagement efforts and support strategies to cultivate alumni partnerships Participate in college and university meetings Identify opportunities for the School to strengthen its campus leadership in public service career pathways and education Collaboration skills are vital for this role as the Student Engagement Specialist will also serve a liaison to numerous university partners. This includes the Liberal Arts Career Enrichment Network and Employer Engagement Specialist, Chaiken Center for Student Success, Office of Digital Pedagogies and Initiatives, Alumni Relations and Development, Office of Government and Community Relations, and Penn State Outreach. Important Note : Travel is also required in this role, mainly in the local area (e.g., to government offices, nonprofit organizations, or events with local leaders). Infrequent regional travel (2 to 3 times a year on average) is also expected, including to Washington, D.C., and Harrisburg. Qualifications: Effective written and verbal communication skills Excellent interpersonal skills; inclusive and respectful when working with others Ability to stay organized with a high attention to detail and accuracy while multi-tasking Outstanding problem-solving skills Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365 or comparable software used to support communication, recordkeeping, document preparation, and spreadsheet management Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and independently with minimal supervision MINIMUM EDUCATION, WORK EXPERIENCE & REQUIRED CERTIFICATIONS Bachelor's Degree 1+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted Required Certifications: None Important Application Instructions : Applicants must submit a cover letter addressing their interest and relevant experience, in addition to a resume. Additional Information: The College of the Liberal Arts is supportive of flexible work arrangements when aligned with the ability to meet the needs of the unit and the essential duties of the position. Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process. In accordance with College guidelines, this position requires a minimum of three days per week of on-site work at the designated work location. BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES Employment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies. This position requires that you operate a motor vehicle as a part of your job duties. A valid driver’s license and successful completion of a motor vehicle records check will be required in addition to standard background checks. Penn State does not sponsor or take over sponsorship of a staff employment Visa. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. SALARY & BENEFITS The salary range for this position, including all possible grades, is $44,628.00 - $64,668.00. Salary Structure - Information on Penn State's salary structure Penn State provides a competitive benefits package for full-time employees designed to support both personal and professional well-being. In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, employees enjoy robust retirement plans and substantial paid time off which includes holidays, vacation and sick time. One of the standout benefits is the generous 75% tuition discount, available to employees as well as eligible spouses and children. For more detailed information, please visit our Benefits Page . CAMPUS SECURITY CRIME STATISTICS Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act and the Pennsylvania Act of 1988, Penn State publishes a combined Annual Security and Annual Fire Safety Report (ASR). The ASR includes crime statistics and institutional policies concerning campus security, such as those concerning alcohol and drug use, crime prevention, the reporting of crimes, sexual assault, and other matters. The ASR is available for review here . EEO IS THE LAW Penn State is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. If you are unable to use our online application process due to an impairment or disability, please contact 814-865-1473. Penn State is committed to and accountable for advancing equity, respect, and belonging. We embrace individual uniqueness, as well as a culture of belonging that supports equity initiatives, leverages the educational and institutional benefits of inclusion in society, and provides opportunities for engagement intended to help all members of the community thrive. We value belonging as a core strength and an essential element of the university’s teaching, research, and service mission. item.title: Part Time Campaign Organizer Flip The Senate
item.description: Part-Time Campaign Organizer – Flip the Senate We are hiring a full-time Campaign Organizer to start immediately and continue through Election Day. The locations are Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. This will expand over the program, so if you are a Nebraskan who lives further away or willing to relocate, please still apply! Who We Are: The Outreach Team is the national engine of campaigners and organizers building a fairer, cleaner, safer, and more peaceful world. We invest in people at every level with industry-leading pay/benefits, rigorous training and support and real paths to leadership. General Overview: Neighbor, it’s your time to step up for Nebraska. We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. Join us on behalf of the Working Class Majority Pac. We are looking for Organizers to talk to voters about an independent candidates run for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team in Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. Organizers will be charged with recruiting, training, and working with a team of volunteers in key counties in Nebraska. The Organizer will start by building and recruiting a team of supporters and volunteers around canvassing. From there, Organizers will continue to engage volunteers through a series of campaign events and actions. What You'll Do: Recruit and Train a Community of Volunteer Activists Call and text supporters and recruit them into grassroots actions. Identify new supporters and volunteers by knocking doors, gathering petitions, flyering, and conducting in-field recruitment efforts in the community and on local campuses. Run grassroots skills training to develop effective campaigners among volunteers. Keep meticulous track of a volunteer list so that no potential volunteer falls through the cracks. Represent the campaign through participation in community spaces and events, while engaging and uplifting coalition and partner organizations. Generate Campaign Actions Gather over a thousand petitions from the community in support of key campaign issues. Recruit and train volunteers to generate more petitions and volunteer engagement at events. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Organize High-Volume Visibility Events Organize and execute exciting, high-visibility in-person events demonstrating support for working families in Nebraska. Educate community members about constituents around affordability and action opportunities and the urgency of continued actions. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training and developing activist leaders in your community to collect supporter petitions, educate others on key campaign issues, and recruit constituents to in-district events and actions. Planning and executing events for constituents around affordability as well as action opportunities including, but not limited to: door knocking, phonebanking, petitioning, visibility events, educational events, and more. Developing relationships with community leaders on corporate accountability, health care, and justice Engaging and expanding our support network through public visibility actions, voter outreach, and relationship-building. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The pay for this position is $26.00 per hour. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

item.title: Selections Coordinator
item.description: Confidential Custom Home Builder Selections Coordinator Location: Greater Richmond, Virginia Are you passionate about residential design and helping homeowners bring their ideas to life? A growing custom home builder in the Greater Richmond area is seeking an organized, creative, and client-focused Design Consultant. If you enjoy combining design expertise, construction knowledge, and exceptional customer service, this could be the opportunity for you! Our client specializes in custom and semi-custom homes and is committed to providing homeowners with a seamless, enjoyable building experience. The company maintains a supportive, team-oriented culture centered on service, integrity, excellence, and having fun while doing meaningful work. As the Design Consultant, you will guide homeowners through finish, color, material, and option selections while ensuring every decision is completed accurately and on schedule. You will collaborate with clients, sales, estimating, production, suppliers, and trade partners to prevent delays and create a polished, well-organized design experience. Key Responsibilities: Guide clients through meetings to select finishes, fixtures, colors, materials, and custom options. Maintain weekly communication with clients throughout the selection process. Manage selection deadlines and explain the scheduling and cost implications of delayed decisions. Keep selection sheets, specifications, pricing, and option documents accurate and current. Prepare change orders, obtain required signatures, and collect applicable client payments. Coordinate with estimating to obtain pricing for custom selections and items outside the standard options catalog. Ensure sales, estimating, production, and field teams receive complete and finalized selection information. Coordinate client meetings with suppliers, subcontractors, and trade partners when appropriate. Complete selections for speculative homes and assist with model-home design decisions. Maintain an organized Design Center with current samples, displays, literature, and product information. Review relevant homeowner documents and design-related responsibilities with clients. Identify and resolve selection issues before they cause delays, errors, or rework. Create engaging social media content featuring design trends, project inspiration, and the custom-home design process. Qualifications: A positive, solutions-focused, "can-do" attitude. Experience in residential design, interior selections, custom homebuilding, construction, or a related client-facing role. Understanding of residential construction processes, materials, finishes, and design coordination. Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple clients, deadlines, and detailed documents. Strong communication, relationship-building, and customer-service skills. Ability to discuss upgrades, pricing, schedules, and design decisions confidently with homeowners. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work through unexpected challenges. Ability to collaborate effectively with sales, estimating, production, suppliers, and trade partners. Strong computer skills and willingness to learn project and selection-management systems. Social media or content-creation experience is an asset. Willingness to work occasional evenings or weekends based on client and project needs. Compensation: Full-time, exempt position. Pay: $75.000 - $95.000 depending on experience Paid time off. 401(k) with company match. Health insurance coverage. Full technology suite. Training and professional-development opportunities. Why Work with Us? Join a growing custom home builder where your creativity, organization, and client-service skills will directly influence the homeowner experience. You will work alongside a collaborative team committed to integrity, continuous improvement, and high-quality results. This is an opportunity to take ownership of the design process, help clients make confident decisions, and contribute to distinctive homes throughout the Greater Richmond area.

item.title: Senior Manager Federal Government Affairs
item.description: When you join Verizon You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife. What you’ll be doing… Verizon is looking for an energetic and proactive advocate to serve as Senior Manager of Federal Government Affairs in our Washington, D.C. office. Representing Verizon before Republican Members of Congress and their staff, you will maintain an active presence across Capitol Hill, execute legislative strategies, and build relationships to inform policy discussions and support Verizon’s business objectives. Responsibilities will include: Developing and maintaining positive relationships with and advocate before Members of Congress and their staffs—actively working receptions, policy events, and Capitol Hill corridors— with lead responsibility for representing Verizon before Republican members of the U.S. House. Managing stakeholder service escalations through conclusion. Coordinating with state government affairs to manage stakeholder inquiries on issues related to the network. Working with internal leadership team to develop VZ’s federal legislative objectives and priorities. Working with external team leads to develop and execute a legislative strategy to achieve specific policy objectives, with a focus on medium and long term strategy. Tracking Congressional activity including: committee hearings and markups as well as floor action on legislative priorities. Coordinating messaging on issues/legislation and for hearings, markups, and floor votes in the House and Senate. What we’re looking for... You'll need to have: Bachelor's degree or four or more years of work experience. Six or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training. Established network of professional relationships with specific line of sight into Congressional Republican politics. Even better if you have one or more of the following: Graduate degree High interpersonal energy and a professional attitude, with demonstrated business acumen and a strong ability to build trust. Ability to solve problems in a sophisticated manner with the ability to understand conflicting dynamics and collaborate on mutually beneficial solutions. Ability to rapidly assess potential risks, benefits and consequences and effectively counsel internal clients concerning business risks. Exceptionally strong written, oral communication, and persuasive advocacy skills. If Verizon and this role sound like a fit for you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification listed above. In this hybrid role, you'll have a defined work location that includes working from home and a minimum of three days per week in the office, which will be set by your manager. Employees are responsible for maintaining compliance with hybrid work policies. Scheduled Weekly Hours 40 Equal Employment Opportunity Verizon is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to veteran status, disability or other legally protected characteristics. Benefits and Compensation Our benefits are designed to help you move forward in your career, and in areas of your life outside of Verizon. From health and wellness benefit options including: medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability, basic life insurance, supplemental life insurance, AD&D insurance, identity theft protection, pet insurance and group home & auto insurance. We also offer a matched 401(k) savings plan, up to 8 company paid holidays per year and up to 6 personal days per year, paid parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition assistance, plus other incentives, we’ve got you covered with our award-winning total rewards package. Depending on the role, employees have the opportunity to receive compensation in the form of premium pay such as overtime, shift differential, holiday pay, allowances, etc. Newly hired employees receive up to 15 days of vacation per year, which grows with additional service. For part-timers, your coverage will vary as you may be eligible for some of these benefits depending on your individual circumstances. The salary will vary depending on your location and confirmed job-related skills and experience. This is an incentive based position with the potential to earn more. For part-time roles, your compensation will be adjusted to reflect your hours. The annual salary range for the location(s) listed on this job requisition based on a full-time schedule is: $120,000.00 - $209,000.00.

item.description: Position Introduction: The Staff Senate and Employee Engagement Program Coordinator serves as a key partner in advancing employee engagement, staff recognition, and Staff Senate initiatives across the University of Oklahoma. This position leads programs, events, communications, and engagement strategies that foster connection, belonging, professional growth, and a positive employee experience. The coordinator serves as a liaison among staff, university leadership, and campus stakeholders, supporting Staff Senate operations while amplifying the voice of staff throughout the institution. The successful candidate will oversee program operations, manage complex projects and events, analyze engagement data, prepare reports and presentations, coordinate budgets and resources, and support committees and collaborative initiatives across the institution. The ideal candidate is an organized, collaborative professional with strong communication and project management skills and a passion for creating a workplace where employees feel valued, connected, and empowered to contribute to the university's success. By combining strategic employee engagement practices with Staff Senate program coordination and advocacy, this position plays a vital role in building a vibrant, inclusive workplace culture that supports the recruitment, retention, engagement, and recognition of OU staff. This role will be responsible for: Supporting and overseeing Staff Senate committees, meetings, and related initiatives Planning, coordinating, and executing Staff Senate, employee engagement, and campus events Managing event logistics, including venue reservations, catering, invitations, vendor coordination, and speaker support Administering Staff Senate fundraising activities and coordinate with university partners on financial and operational processes serving as a liaison between Staff Senate, Human Resources, university leadership, and campus stakeholders Other duties as assigned. Equivalent/Substitution: Will accept 48 months of experience in lieu of a Bachelor's degree to equal 96 months of related experience. Required Certifications and Licenses: None Department Preferences: Experience in employee engagement, event planning, program coordination, or higher education administration. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholder relationships. Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication abilities. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other business software applications.

item.title: Assistant Professor Political Science
item.description: APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS: CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process . Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday. CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday. Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants . POSITION SPECIFICS The Department of Political Science at The Pennsylvania State University, University Park, PA, USA, invites applications for a full-time tenure-track position, at the rank of Assistant Professor . The Department invites applications from scholars in any political science subfield whose research and teaching examine the intersection of artificial intelligence and politics and who can offer undergraduate and graduate courses in political methodology, including causal inference. Relevant areas of research and teaching include, but are not limited to, the uses of AI by governments, politicians, or candidates; the effects of AI on political institutions, disinformation, public discourse, or political behavior; the regulation of AI technologies; the political economy or geopolitics of AI; the role of AI in political violence and its effects on democracy; or the development of social science methodologies related to artificial intelligence. The Assistant Professor will have demonstrated ability as a researcher and a promising research agenda with a focus on artificial intelligence and political science. The candidate should show potential for excellence in instruction and mentoring at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Promise for securing external research funding is also desirable. This position will include resident and online teaching and normal university service. The teaching load during the academic year is four courses. Onsite teaching is an essential function of this job. Duties will involve a combination of teaching, research, and service, based on the candidate’s qualifications. A Ph.D. in Political Science or related field is required by the appointment date. Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until an applicant is selected. Interested candidates must submit an online application at Penn State’s Job Posting Board , and should upload the following application materials electronically: a letter of interest, CV or resume, a writing sample, and a list of three references with contact information. Inquiries may be directed to Paige McCarthy, Assistant to the Head of Political Science ( pem5220@psu.edu ). Visit our website at https://polisci.la.psu.edu/ for more information on our department. BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES Employment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies. BENEFITS Penn State provides a competitive benefits package for full-time employees designed to support both personal and professional wellbeing. In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, employees enjoy robust retirement plans. One of the standout benefits is the generous 75% tuition discount, available to employees as well as eligible spouses and children. For more detailed information, please visit our Benefits Page. (Note: For Postdoctoral benefits, please see our Postdoctoral Benefits page.) CAMPUS SECURITY CRIME STATISTICS Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act and the Pennsylvania Act of 1988, Penn State publishes a combined Annual Security and Annual Fire Safety Report (ASR). The ASR includes crime statistics and institutional policies concerning campus security, such as those concerning alcohol and drug use, crime prevention, the reporting of crimes, sexual assault, and other matters. The ASR is available for review here . EEO IS THE LAW Penn State is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. If you are unable to use our online application process due to an impairment or disability, please contact 814-865-1473. Penn State is committed to and accountable for advancing equity, respect, and belonging. We embrace individual uniqueness, as well as a culture of belonging that supports equity initiatives, leverages the educational and institutional benefits of inclusion in society, and provides opportunities for engagement intended to help all members of the community thrive. We value belonging as a core strength and an essential element of the university’s teaching, research, and service mission. item.title: Director Public Policy
item.description: Job Duties: Identifies and analyzes key regulatory and policy initiatives in the Asia-Pacific region affecting the global fund industry and the impacts of such developments on ICI member firms in Chinese (Cantonese and/or Mandarin) and English. Develops recommendations and policy positions on key proposals and initiatives in the Asia Pacific region and leads the drafting of relevant position papers and other materials, working in collaboration with ICI members and other ICI departments as appropriate. Designs and implements engagement and advocacy strategies with regulators and policymakers in support of ICI advocacy activities in the Asia Pacific region. Briefs ICI staff and ICI members on regulatory and policy developments through written and oral communications, including member memos, webinars, and other products. Prepares briefings for the CEO, Chief Global Affairs Officer, and the MD for Asia and Global Analytics on key topics and in support of meetings with senior officials and other key stakeholders in Asia Pacific. Designs and executes webinars, roundtables, and other member events in Asia Pacific, including identifying relevant discussion topics, securing public official and expert speakers, managing logistics, and ensuring seamless execution. Develops content and talking points on APAC and EMEA issues for ICI senior leaders' participation in external seminars, luncheons, and other public speaking engagements. Builds relationships with regulators, policymakers, and key stakeholders (e.g., local industry associations) in the Asia Pacific region in Chinese (Cantonese and/or Mandarin) and English. Supports structuring of effective and efficient meetings of ICI steering and policy committees for Asia-based members, and topic-specific working groups, including developing agendas and leading relevant discussion items. Helps to ensure the accuracy and reliability of information and analysis collected and used in ICI materials. Drafts final reports of research results for internal use and use in ICI publications. Works effectively with external consultants and vendors to support ICI projects and ICI goals. Performs other duties as assigned. Requirements: Bachelor’s in Business, Finance, Economics, or related and 96 months of experience in the job offered or as an analyst or researcher in the asset management, or financial regulatory space. Alternatively, will accept a Master’s degree and 60 months of experience in the positions listed above. Additionally, all candidates must possess written and spoken fluency in English and Chinese (Cantonese or Mandarin). Reference check. Must have 5 years of: 1) knowledge of APAC financial institutions and financial markets; 2) experience independently managing multiple workflows against tight deadlines; and 3) experience collaborating with and presenting to colleagues and consultants, across regions, jurisdictions, and time zones. Also, must have 3 years of: 1) experience synthesizing information, analysis, and data to respond to queries from members and from policymakers; and 2) analyzing the impacts of regulatory initiatives and policy issues on the asset management industry in Asia, and translating industry concerns into policy positions and advocacy strategy, and then executing the strategy. Position is based out of 1401 H St. NW, Suite 1200, Washington, DC 20005. Must travel to Asia-Pacific region, Europe, and domestically throughout the year. Typically travels to Asia a minimum of 6 times per year to meet with Asia members. Partial remote schedule: 3 days in office and 2 days WFH (work from home) with Tuesday and Wednesday core in-office days. Also, ability to work outside US business hours (Monday-Friday 9am-5pm) as needed for meetings with Asia members. Rate of Pay: $174,450.00-$189,300.00/year.

item.title: Staff Writer Congressional Leadership
item.description: Staff Writer, Congressional Leadership FiscalNote Washington, District of Columbia, United States Full-time 3 days ago $75,000 - $80,000 USD yearly About the Position CQ Roll Call seeks an experienced, versatile and motivated journalist to join a team of reporters covering the elected leadership of the House factions, caucuses and group dynamics. This is a role for someone who can generate distinctive coverage for a sophisticated audience. The ideal candidate has excellent news judgment, superior writing and reporting skills, and a strong record of breaking news and developing sources. You can connect the dots and can balance spot news and unique enterprise. Experience covering Congress strongly preferred. About the CQ Roll Call Team Washington’s CQ Roll Call brings up-to-date news, analysis and insights to senior decision-makers on Capitol Hill. This trusted source of unbiased, impartial information provides authoritative, nonpartisan and accurate congressional news and legislative tracking tools to its subscribers. Through more than 40 print and online products, CQ Roll Call offers insight on the people and institutions that influence public policy and legislation, keeping readers updated on a weekly, daily and real-time basis with coverage of every legislative action in Congress via breaking news, bill tracking and member profiles. About You You report and write for a sophisticated audience interested in politics and policy, pursuing the truth from a variety of sources and reflecting their positions with impartiality. Collaborative yet independent, you know when to work with colleagues and when to break out stories on your own. You uphold the highest professional and ethical standards, probing beneath the surface of official statements to uncover the deeper story. Committed to continuous professional growth and engagement within a broader community of journalists, you contribute meaningfully to the shared goals and success of the newsroom team. Application Requirements: All applicants must submit four (4) published writing samples from newspapers, news websites or news magazines that demonstrate reporting and writing ability. When submitting stories, please include a note about your work: What sets it apart from other coverage? What does it illustrate about your approach to journalism? The work samples can be uploaded as documents or provided as direct links that are not password-protected. The position is based in Washington, DC and requires daily reporting from the Capitol. The base salary range for this position is $75,000 - 80,000 per year. #LI-HR1 What to Expect in This Role Producing a daily story of the day about congressional leaders and their strategies and messaging, as well as contributing to other teams’ stories and medium- and long-term enterprise reports Thriving in a newsroom where journalism is produced for two websites, one subscriber-focused on policy, and the other a broader political audience; a newspaper that publishes when Congress is in session; and dozens of newsletters in front of and behind a paywall Contributing to both CQ and Roll Call newsletters as well as prominent space in Roll Call print, contributing to legislative tracking as needed (markups and vote entry) as well as major legislation and nominations Writing and analysis of annual CQ Vote Studies reports Working with the White House correspondent on the relationship between the executive and legislative leaders Collaborating on photo/visuals, graphics, podcasts and other storytelling forms to enhance your reporting Writing profile stories about members of the House and Senate, particularly leaders and prominent caucus and faction leaders and other lawmakers and congressional candidates that feed CQ’s Guide to the New Congress and other products about members Participating in webinars and other corporate activities to amplify your journalism What Sets You Apart 3+ years of experience as a reporter at newspapers, news websites, magazines, wire services and other news outlets. Experience in Washington, D.C., for a subscription news outlet, wire service or news bureau covering Congress is strongly recommended An ability to find new, creative ways to scrutinize the relationships among Congress, the White House, judicial branch and lobbying efforts to influence them A college degree is helpful but not essential. Equivalent, relevant work experience is what matters Strong written and verbal communication skills and mastery of AP style Strong understanding of congressional procedure and history and culture and the ability to convey your passion for the subject to readers A commitment to the journalistic values of accuracy, objectivity, fairness and editorial independence Excited about this role, but don't meet 100% of the expected qualifications listed above? We'd still love for you to apply! When applying to FiscalNote, rest assured that your application is reviewed by a living, breathing human being and evaluated based on key competencies needed for success in the position. Our Recruiting team maintains awareness of all open roles which means your application may be assessed against multiple positions and we will reach out to gauge your interest in other opportunities as appropriate. Questions or concerns? Contact recruiting.team @fiscalnote.com, we'd be happy to connect! As part of FiscalNote's commitment to creating an accessible and inclusive hiring process, we strive to provide reasonable accommodations for persons with medical conditions or disabilities that will enable their access to the hiring process. If you need an accommodation, please send an email to recruiting.team @fiscalnote.com to let us know the nature of your request. About FiscalNote FiscalNote (NYSE: NOTE) is a leader in policy and global intelligence. By uniquely combining data, technology, and insights, FiscalNote empowers customers with critical insights and the tools to turn them into action. Home to CQ, FrontierView, VoterVoice, and many other industry-leading brands, FiscalNote helps organizations stay ahead of political and business risk. At FiscalNote, We Lead with Values Know your Audience ∙ Find the Truth ∙ Drive Alignment ∙ Level Up ∙ Own the Job ∙ Bias for Action ∙ Support the Family Company Benefits FiscalNote supports our people by enabling team members with flexibility and benefits to promote well-being and balance, ensuring all FiscalNoters can bring their authentic selves to work. We start by offering competitive salaries, retirement accounts, and equity packages to ensure we’re all FN owners. Plus, our comprehensive benefits packages align with regional requirements and expectations no matter where you are located across the globe. Learn more at https://careers.fiscalnote.com/benefits/ . FiscalNote values diversity. We are committed to equal opportunities and creating an inclusive environment for all our employees. We welcome applicants regardless of ethnic origin, national origin, gender, race, religious beliefs, disability, sexual orientation or age. FiscalNote is an EEOC employer. FiscalNote uses E-Verify to confirm the employment eligibility of all new employees. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit www.DHS.gov/E-Verify . Washington, District of Columbia, United States $75,000 - $80,000 USD yearly

item.description: Department/Organization 204691 - Political Science Rank Assistant Professor Position Summary The Department of Political Science invites applications for a tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level in Comparative Politics, beginning August 16, 2027 Detailed Position Information The Department of Political Science invites applications for a tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level in Comparative Politics, beginning August 16, 2027. The successful candidate should have a strong research agenda that applies rigorous methods to important theoretical questions, with a clear plan for peer-reviewed publication. The position is open to candidates with any theoretical or regional expertise, and the successful candidate will play an active role in undergraduate teaching and the graduate program. The University of Alabama is a student-centered research university and the flagship campus of the University of Alabama System. The Political Science Department offers B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. degrees. A completed Ph.D. in political science or a closely related field is required for appointment at the level of Assistant Professor. Review of applications will begin September 21, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. Minimum Qualifications Ph.D. in political science or a closely related field is required for appointment at the level of Assistant Professor. Preferred Qualifications Instructions and Required Materials for Application To apply, go to facultyjobs.ua.edu and complete the online application. Attach a cover letter and curriculum vitae. Additional materials — including a research statement, writing samples, and teaching materials — along with transcripts and three letters of recommendation, will be requested from finalists. Review of applications will begin September 21, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. For more information, contact Christopher Hale, Search Committee Chair, at cwhale@ua.edu, or the Department of Political Science, Box 870213, Tuscaloosa, AL 35487-0213. About the Division/College/School The J. Frank Barefield Jr. College of Arts and Sciences at The University of Alabama offers an exciting and dynamic environment for faculty seeking to make an impact in their field and in the lives of the innovators and changemakers of tomorrow. As the largest college at The University, we house over 9,000 students and 1,000 faculty and staff across our 22 departments. With nationally recognized programs and award-winning faculty, our College has positioned itself as a leader in higher education. Our facilities and resources include state-of-the-art laboratories, research centers, and performance venues, providing students with hands-on learning experiences and opportunities for research and creative expression. The College is committed to the liberal arts philosophy that fosters creative and critical thinking and a lifetime of learning.” About the University The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation. In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country. UA was recently recognized as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. students for the seventh time in nine years, as well as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. Scholars for the first time. UA is one of only 12 universities in the nation to receive both honors. For reasons like this, the University made Forbes list of America’s Top Colleges for 2023 and Time magazine’s list of Top 50 Best Colleges for Future Leaders. It also made Princeton Review’s list of Top Value Colleges. UA is also designated among the top doctoral research universities in the United States in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. One of the fastest growing major research institutions in the nation, UA saw a 21% increase in sponsored awards in the 2023 fiscal year. Since 2015, UA has invested over $1.1 billion in the physical campus, adding more than 2.55 million gross square feet of space, over 150 new research-intensive faculty, signature research areas (e.g., “The Alabama Research Institutes”), and a growing number of partnerships with industry and with state and federal agencies. The University employs nearly 2,100 faculty and over 4,500 staff, with 52 UA researchers included in the National Academy of Inventors. An additional 40 current faculty have received the NSF CAREER Award, the nation’s most prestigious recognition of top performing young scientists in disciplines ranging from nanoscience and engineering to biological sciences. Detailed Position Information The Department of Political Science invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Public Administration, beginning August 16, 2027. The successful candidate will take an active role in the department’s graduate Master of Public Administration (MPA) program and contribute to undergraduate teaching. While we welcome applicants from all subfields of public administration, we are particularly interested in candidates with research and teaching interests in public budgeting, financial management, or nonprofit management. Review of applications will begin on September 21, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. For more information, please contact the search committee chair, Hyunjung Ji, at hji4@ua.edu. Minimum Qualifications A completed Ph.D. in public administration, public policy, political science, or a closely related field is required at the time of appointment. Candidates should demonstrate a strong research agenda with a clear trajectory for peer-reviewed scholarly publication. Preferred Qualifications Instructions and Required Materials for Application To apply, please visit https://facultyjobs.ua.edu. Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, research and teaching statements, and the names and contact information of three professional references. Finalists will be asked to provide additional materials, including official transcripts and letters of recommendation. Review of applications will begin on September 21, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. For more information, please contact the search committee chair, Hyunjung Ji, at hji4@ua.edu. About the Division/College/School The J. Frank Barefield Jr. College of Arts and Sciences at The University of Alabama offers an exciting and dynamic environment for faculty seeking to make an impact in their field and in the lives of the innovators and changemakers of tomorrow. As the largest college at The University, we house over 9,000 students and 1,000 faculty and staff across our 22 departments. With nationally recognized programs and award-winning faculty, our College has positioned itself as a leader in higher education. Our facilities and resources include state-of-the-art laboratories, research centers, and performance venues, providing students with hands-on learning experiences and opportunities for research and creative expression. The College is committed to the liberal arts philosophy that fosters creative and critical thinking and a lifetime of learning.” About the University The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation. In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country. UA was recently recognized as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. students for the seventh time in nine years, as well as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. Scholars for the first time. UA is one of only 12 universities in the nation to receive both honors. For reasons like this, the University made Forbes list of America’s Top Colleges for 2023 and Time magazine’s list of Top 50 Best Colleges for Future Leaders. It also made Princeton Review’s list of Top Value Colleges. UA is also designated among the top doctoral research universities in the United States in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. One of the fastest growing major research institutions in the nation, UA saw a 21% increase in sponsored awards in the 2023 fiscal year. Since 2015, UA has invested over $1.1 billion in the physical campus, adding more than 2.55 million gross square feet of space, over 150 new research-intensive faculty, signature research areas (e.g., “The Alabama Research Institutes”), and a growing number of partnerships with industry and with state and federal agencies. The University employs nearly 2,100 faculty and over 4,500 staff, with 52 UA researchers included in the National Academy of Inventors. An additional 40 current faculty have received the NSF CAREER Award, the nation’s most prestigious recognition of top performing young scientists in disciplines ranging from nanoscience and engineering to biological sciences. A prior conviction reported as a result of the background investigation DOES NOT automatically disqualify a candidate from consideration for this position. A candidate with a prior conviction or negative behavioral red flags will receive an individualized review of the prior conviction or negative behavioral red flags before a hiring decision is made. item.title: Government Affairs 7610
item.description: Description Are you looking for an opportunity with plenty of growth potential? Do you enjoy working in an exciting, fast-paced, collaborative environment? Are you interested in working with the world’s most innovative companies to create a more connected world? Connecting Continents. Impacting Communities. The backbone of the Internet is a series of high-tech subsea fiber optic cables deployed throughout the globe - SubCom has deployed over 50% of them. Our employees ensure data communications networks are engineered, manufactured, deployed to the highest standards, enabling faster and more reliable connectivity to communities worldwide. Every member of the SubCom team plays a role in an end-to-end process that is critical to enterprises, governments, big cities, and rural towns. We encourage, expect, and value creativity, thoughtful risk taking, openness to change, and diverse perspectives. Whether you’re a seasoned applicant seeking a new and exciting challenge, or you’re new to the workforce and looking for a flexible, rewarding, and fast-paced position with an innovative and stable organization (since 1953), SubCom has opportunities to advance your career. Position Overview The Government Affairs role serves as SubCom's senior liaison to U.S. executive and legislative agencies, the intelligence community, regulatory bodies, and key foreign governments. The role monitors and influences telecommunications, infrastructure, security, and maritime policy; advances regulatory and legislative outcomes that support SubCom's business objectives; strengthens SubCom's position as a trusted provider of secure undersea cable infrastructure; and helps identify and pursue government-funded business opportunities. Responsibilities Build and maintain strategic relationships with U.S. executive branch agencies and politically appointed officials to understand policy priorities and assess implications for SubCom's strategy and operations. Advise senior SubCom leaders on current and emerging federal policies, regulations, security priorities, and geopolitical developments affecting global communications infrastructure. Advance regulatory policies that support fair market competition, efficient approvals, and SubCom's business and financial objectives, including engagement in the Team Telecom and Federal Communications Commission licensing processes. Engage with Congress and legislative officials to shape laws, treaties, and international agreements affecting undersea cable installation, maintenance, repair, and related vessel operations. Maintain relationships with U.S. intelligence and security agencies to monitor industry threats, communicate SubCom's capabilities, and support recognition of SubCom as a trusted partner in global communications infrastructure. Partner with Legal and senior leadership to support compliance with U.S. and foreign laws and regulations governing undersea cable infrastructure and services. Develop and expand relationships with key foreign governments and participate in bilateral and multilateral policy discussions to advance trusted and secure undersea cable networks. Lead cross-functional initiatives that align SubCom's security practices, supply chain strategy, and external positioning with government expectations for trusted and secure infrastructure providers. Identify and help shape government-funded programs related to undersea cable infrastructure; partner with Sales and industry participants to position SubCom for funding opportunities and compliant project delivery. Consistently ensure that business is conducted with integrity and that behavior aligns with SubCom policies, procedures, and core values. Qualifications Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Minimum of 12 years of progressive regulatory or government affairs experience in telecommunications, including regular direct engagement with U.S. executive branch agencies and senior government officials. Expert knowledge of U.S. and foreign government policies and regulations related to telecommunications infrastructure, national security, and undersea cable systems. Demonstrated ability to influence federal policy, regulatory, or legislative outcomes affecting the undersea cable industry. Demonstrated experience securing significant federal funding for infrastructure programs and overseeing funding compliance through project completion. Expert knowledge of international multilateral processes and experience representing a company or government in bilateral and multilateral negotiations. Ability to translate complex political, regulatory, security, and geopolitical developments into clear business implications and recommendations for senior leaders. Exceptional written and verbal communication, relationship-building, negotiation, judgment, and influencing skills. Ability to lead cross-functional work, manage multiple priorities, and operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly visible environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook. NOTE : This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employee may perform other related duties as negotiated to meet the ongoing needs of the organization. Candidates for positions with SubCom must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Employment eligibility verification will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Our selection procedure is based on local, state and federal law. Please be sure to attach a resume to your application. We are not able to consider applications without a resume. BENEFITS SubCom offers a comprehensive benefits package, including but not limited to: competitive salaries, medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance coverages, FSA, HSA, generous vacation, paid sick leave, paid parental leave, paid holidays, tuition reimbursement, adoption assistance, and a 401(k) plan with generous company match. Additionally, some positions may be eligible for shift differential. AFFIRMATIVE ACTION/EQUAL EMPLOYER OPPORTUNITY SubCom is committed to providing a work environment that prohibits discrimination based on age, color, disability, ethnicity, marital status, national origin, race, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability or any other characteristics protected by applicable law or regulation. SubCom engineers, manufactures, and installs subsea fiber optic data cables - the unsung heroes of global communication. With an unrelenting focus on quality, reliability, and value, SubCom offers flexible end-to-end building blocks for the high-tech networks that are the backbone of the world's digital infrastructure. While the company's origins date back to the mid-19 th century, SubCom has deployed enough cable to circle the equator more than 25 times since its entry into the communications industry in 1955. SUBCOM’S CORE VALUES Quality - Accountability - Teamwork - Innovation

item.title: Campaign Organizer Come To Nebraska Defeat Pete Ricketts Flip The Senate
item.description: Campaign Organizer- Nebraska Location and Timeline: We are hiring a full-time Campaign Organizer to begin by the end of August and continue through Election Day. The locations are Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. This will expand over the program, so if you are a Nebraskan who lives further away or willing to relocate, please still apply! Who We Are: The Outreach Team is the national engine of campaigners and organizers building a fairer, cleaner, safer, and more peaceful world. We invest in people at every level with industry-leading pay/benefits, rigorous training and support and real paths to leadership. General Overview: Neighbor, it’s your time to step up for Nebraska. We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. Join us on behalf of the Working Class Majority Pac. We are looking for Organizers to talk to voters about Dan Osborn’s run for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team in Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. Organizers will be charged with recruiting, training, and working with a team of volunteers in key counties in Nebraska. The Organizer will start by building and recruiting a team of supporters and volunteers around canvassing. From there, Organizers will continue to engage volunteers through a series of campaign events and actions. Requirements: Valid driver's license and Insurance as well as a verifiable record of safe driving. Must be over 21 (in order to drive the rental car if needed) Must be available full-time. What You'll Do: Recruit and Train a Community of Volunteer Activists Call and text supporters and recruit them into grassroots actions. Identify new supporters and volunteers by knocking doors, gathering petitions, flyering, and conducting in-field recruitment efforts in the community and on local campuses. Run grassroots skills training to develop effective campaigners among volunteers. Keep meticulous track of a volunteer list so that no potential volunteer falls through the cracks. Represent the campaign through participation in community spaces and events, while engaging and uplifting coalition and partner organizations. Generate Campaign Actions Gather over a thousand petitions from the community in support of key campaign issues. Recruit and train volunteers to generate more petitions and volunteer engagement at events. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Organize High-Volume Visibility Events Organize and execute exciting, high-visibility in-person events demonstrating support for working families in Nebraska. Educate community members about constituents around affordability and action opportunities and the urgency of continued actions. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training and developing activist leaders in your community to collect supporter petitions, educate others on key campaign issues, and recruit constituents to in-district events and actions. Planning and executing events for constituents around affordability as well as action opportunities including, but not limited to: door knocking, phonebanking, petitioning, visibility events, educational events, and more. Developing relationships with community leaders on corporate accountability, health care, and justice Engaging and expanding our support network through public visibility actions, voter outreach, and relationship-building. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The salary for this position is $55,000 to $67,000 for full-time. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

item.title: Legislative Liaison
item.description: The Christian Business Partnership’s Legislative Liaison works for the Executive Director of The Partnership in serving as Christian business owners’ lead voice at the Ohio Statehouse and with lawmakers. His or her mission is to vigorously champion the religious freedom of Christian business owners while fostering a robust and open marketplace where innovation and competition allow every entrepreneur to succeed. Professional, personable, highly-organized, and deeply passionate about the Gospel and The Partnership’s mission, the Legislative Liaison plays an essential role in serving Christian business owners in Ohio. Reports to : Christian Business Partnership Executive Director Hours : Monday–Friday, 8:00am to 4:30pm Compensation : Full-time, Salaried/Exempt Location : CCV Office in Columbus, Ohio, with Occasional Statewide Travel Benefits : PTO (Paid Time Off), 10 Paid Holidays, Monthly Cell Phone Allotment, Mileage, Health, Vision, and Dental Insurance (CCV covers 75% of premium), Life Insurance, 4% Match on Retirement Plan Available after 1 Year Key Responsibilities Lead The Partnership’s efforts to advance legislative priorities at the Ohio Statehouse. Prepare and give legislative testimony in support of bills on The Partnership’s legislative agenda or in opposition to bills that undermine our mission. Stay “in-the-know” about issues facing Ohio’s communities, and especially Christianowned businesses. Conduct legislative research including reviewing legislation & amendments introduced in the General Assembly for impact on The Partnership’s issues. Draft Fact Sheets on The Partnership’s primary bills. Present The Partnership’s mission and information on issues at public speaking engagements and with the media. Provide periodic analysis and reports for management. Other duties as assigned. Job Qualifications & Requirements Skills and Experience Undergraduate degree required. 3-5 years of experience in policy-related field and knowledge of Ohio legislative process preferred. Strong research skills as well as proven verbal and written communication skills. Attentive to detail and well organized. Strong time management skills, punctual, able to operate on a schedule, meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects simultaneously. Flexible to accommodate shifting priorities. Ability to thrive in a multi-tasking, fast-paced work environment. Self-motivated daily by a passion to see The Partnership's work advance . Able to be proactive and strive to close gaps in skill and knowledge. Proficient in Google, Microsoft programs, and CRM database. Character and Spiritual Mature Christian, currently attending or pursuing attendance in a local church. Agreement with and adherence to CCV’s Statement of Faith and Code of Conduct. Demonstrated commitment to CCV’s mission and position on Core Issues. Ability to work discreetly with confidential information. Trustworthy, responsible, tactful, diplomatic, and focused on building consensus rather than emphasizing differences. Maintain a high level of professionalism focused on client/constituent relationships.
item.dc:creator: CCV

item.title: Senior Director Government Affairs
item.description: Description Oracle Corporate Affairs is seeking a Senior Director, Government Affairs . The Senior Director will report to the Senior Vice President, Government Affairs . In collaboration with a diverse portfolio of internal and external stakeholders, the Senior Director will serve as one of the company’s Legislative and Executive Branch lobbyists and a key advisor to senior company leaders. Working in close partnership with his / her government affairs colleagues, specific business units, and other relevant functional experts within the company, the candidate will identify, prioritize and lead advocacy efforts to drive domestic legislative, policy, and business initiatives. The ideal candidate understands the importance of the role to the success of the organization; has a robust understanding of information technology across a broad spectrum of business and policy priorities; has demonstrated success in achieving results in support of specific initiatives and objectives; and is experienced in working with the Democratic party. The Senior Director will be based in Washington, DC, and will be expected to primarily perform their duties as an in-office employee. Career Level - IC 5 Responsibilities QUALIFICATIONS DESIRED SKILLS Understanding of information technology policies. Experience in political giving strategies and working with corporate political action committees. Detail oriented, organized, and driven to follow-through and complete tasks. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, including experience with conceptualizing and leading projects independently with minimal supervision. Commitment to acting at all times with the highest integrity, including strict adherence to applicable laws and company values, which go beyond legal compliance. Qualifications Disclaimer: Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements. Range and benefit information provided in this posting are specific to the stated locations only US: Hiring Range in USD from: $114,600 to $234,600 per annum. May be eligible for bonus, equity, and compensation deferral. Oracle maintains broad salary ranges for its roles in order to account for variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions and locations, as well as reflect Oracle's differing products, industries and lines of business. Candidates are typically placed into the range based on the preceding factors as well as internal peer equity. Oracle US offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes the following: 1. Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including expert medical opinion 2. Short term disability and long term disability 3. Life insurance and AD&D 4. Supplemental life insurance (Employee/Spouse/Child) 5. Health care and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts 6. Pre-tax commuter and parking benefits 7. 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company match 8. Paid time off: Flexible Vacation is provided to all eligible employees assigned to a salaried (non-overtime eligible) position. Accrued Vacation is provided to all other employees eligible for vacation benefits. For employees working at least 35 hours per week, the vacation accrual rate is 13 days annually for the first three years of employment and 18 days annually for subsequent years of employment. Vacation accrual is prorated for employees working between 20 and 34 hours per week. Employees working fewer than 20 hours per week are not eligible for vacation. 9. 11 paid holidays 10. Paid sick leave: 72 hours of paid sick leave upon date of hire. Refreshes each calendar year. Unused balance will carry over each year up to a maximum cap of 112 hours. 11. Paid parental leave 12. Adoption assistance 13. Employee Stock Purchase Plan 14. Financial planning and group legal 15.
