item.title: Community Legislative Liaison Bureau Of Government Affairs
item.description: The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (The Health Department) protects and promotes the health of eight million New Yorkers with a budget of $2 billion, and roughly 7,000 staff. Central to this effort are programs that combat communicable diseases, expand access to health care, provide maternal health support, surveil human health conditions from chronic disease to mental health and substance use issues, and tackle other public health challenges. Pursuing effective public health policy is also vital to this work. The Legislative Affairs unit within the Bureau of Government Affairs plays a central role in DOHMH's ability to fulfil its mission by developing the agency's legislative agenda at the City, State and Federal levels, serving as the agency's point of contact for elected officials and coordinating legislative discussions with the Mayor's office and other City agencies. The Bureau also coordinates the Department's appearance at public hearings; maintain relationships with advocacy groups, civic organizations and lobbyists; and coordinates with the agency's press office and communications teams on external communications and events. The Community Affairs Unit helps the Department maintain good relations with elected officials, community boards, civic organizations, and other stakeholders by responding quickly and accurately to requests for information, organizing speakers for community events, problem solving and informing members of Department initiatives. The Legislative Affairs and Community Affairs units in the Office of External Affairs within the Bureau of Government Affairs seek to hire a Community Legislative Liaison. DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Respond in a timely, concise, and intelligible fashion to inquiries from local elected officials, community boards and the general public - Attend and represent the Department at community board meetings, town halls, public meetings in response to day-to-day operations and public health emergencies - Disseminate public health information to community stakeholders and the public - Provides staffing and supporting role to the Public Information Office (PIO) during public health emergency activations - Participates in public health emergency trainings - Coordinate logistics of convening community/public forums and meetings with other city agencies and stake holders (e.g. hospitals) - Research, track, and analyze legislation and coordinate the department’s response in areas that may include the Office of Emergency Preparedness, Center for Population Health Data Science federal affairs, and other program areas as needed. - Prep executive-level leadership in the agency for public hearings and meetings with elected officials. - Cultivate and maintain relationships with other organizational units within the Health Department and other key partners. - Assist in developing and implementing legislative strategies. - Serve as a liaison to the Mayor’s Office by representing the Department’s position on public health issues and coordinating with internal partners. - Investigate and respond to elected official requests regarding general information on Health Department programs or actions. - Develop briefing materials and other content with research data and reports for the city council, state legislature, and federal government. - Maintenance of other internal unit and/or division organizational systems. - Respond in a timely, concise, and intelligible fashion to inquiries from local elected officials, community boards, and the general public - Special projects as assigned by the director PREFERRED SKILLS: - Excellent analytical, political, and writing skills. - Experience working in government and/or intergovernmental/legislative affairs. - Academic background in political science, public policy, public health, or related field. - Spreadsheets, Airtable, and data-tracking skills. - Must be self-motivated, able to work on multiple responsibilities simultaneously, and share the agency’s commitment to public health. Why you should work for us: - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. For more information, please visit the U.S. Department of Education’s website (https://studentaid.gov/pslf/) - Benefits: City employees are entitled to unmatched benefits such as: o a premium-free health insurance plan that saves employees over $10K annually, per a 2024 assessment. o additional health, fitness, and financial benefits may be available based on the position’s associated union/benefit fund. o a public sector defined benefit pension plan with steady monthly payments in retirement. o a tax-deferred savings program and o a robust Worksite Wellness Program that offers resources and opportunities to keep you healthy while serving New Yorkers. - Work From Home Policy: Depending on your position, you may be able to work up to two days during the week from home. - Job Security - you could enjoy more job security compared to private sector employment and be able to contribute to making NYC a healthy place to live and work. Established in 1805, the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC Health Department) is the oldest and largest health department in the U.S., dedicated to protecting and improving the health of NYC. Our mission is to safeguard the health of every resident and cultivate a city where everyone, regardless of age, background, or location, can achieve their optimal health. We provide a wide array of programs and services focused on food and nutrition, anti-tobacco support, chronic disease prevention, HIV/AIDS treatment, family and child health, environmental health, mental health, and social justice initiatives. As the primary population health strategist and policy authority for NYC, with a rich history of public health initiatives and scientific advancements, from addressing the 1822 yellow fever outbreak to the COVID-19 pandemic, we serve as a global leader in public health innovation and expertise. Come join us and help to continue our efforts in making a difference in the lives of all New Yorkers! item.title: Senior Administrative Assistant Government Affairs
item.description: Job Description General Summary: The Senior Administrative Assistant will serve as a trusted administrative partner to the Vice President, U.S. Government Affairs & Patient Advocacy; the Vice President, Federal Government Affairs; and the Executive Director, State Government Affairs. The role is responsible for complex calendar and travel management, meeting and event coordination, contracting and invoice administration, executive preparedness, and broader team operations. The successful candidate will work with a high degree of independence, judgment, discretion, and attention to detail while managing competing priorities and interacting professionally with senior internal and external stakeholders. Key Duties and Responsibilities: Executive and Stakeholder Support Serve as a primary administrative point of contact for supported leaders, anticipating needs, applying sound judgment, and appropriately screening, routing, prioritizing, and escalating requests. Build effective working relationships with senior executives, administrative colleagues, external consultants, government officials and their staff, trade associations, patient advocacy organizations, vendors, and other stakeholders. Handle confidential, sensitive, and time-critical information with discretion and professionalism. Complex Calendar Management Proactively manage complex and frequently changing calendars in Microsoft Outlook, including scheduling across multiple leaders, functions, sites, time zones, and external organizations. Resolve conflicts based on business priorities, protect time for critical work, and communicate scheduling tradeoffs and changes promptly. Ensure leaders have appropriate preparation time, meeting materials, locations, technology, and logistical information. Travel and Expense Administration Use Concur to independently arrange domestic and international travel, including air, ground transportation, lodging, itineraries, and other required logistics. Prepare and process accurate, timely expense reports and related correspondence; manage reimbursement inquiries and coordinate with travel agencies, airlines, hotels, and internal partners. Monitor and resolve time-sensitive travel and logistical issues during business travel, exercising judgment regarding when escalation is required. Contracting, Procurement, and Invoicing Coordinate the end-to-end administrative workflow for consultant and vendor agreements through Coupa and Icertis, including intake, routing, approvals, signatures, purchase orders, Statements of Work, invoicing, payment status, and record maintenance. Partner with Legal, Procurement, Finance, business owners, and external firms to support timely and compliant contracting and payment processes. Support vendor onboarding, invoice reconciliation, payment tracking, and basic departmental budget administration. Meetings, Conferences, and Events Plan and coordinate recurring team meetings, leadership meetings, conferences, off-sites, dinners, and external engagements. Manage venue sourcing, attendee communications, catering, transportation, audiovisual and technology needs, vendor coordination, on-site logistics, contracts, payments, and expense reconciliation, as applicable; integrate with Corporate Services as needed. Coordinate activities in accordance with company meeting, expense, procurement, and compliance requirements. Executive Preparedness and Document Support Develop agendas, gather and distribute pre-read materials, maintain organized reference files, and track administrative follow-ups and action items. Support the preparation, proofreading, formatting, and distribution of presentations, correspondence, reports, and other business documents. Help ensure supported leaders are prepared for meetings, travel, and external engagements while appropriately distinguishing administrative support from substantive government affairs content ownership. Team and Department Operations Support recurring business routines, team communications, shared calendars and resources, distribution and contact lists, onboarding and offboarding, office access, technology, facilities, and supply needs. Lead or support administrative and operational projects requiring coordination across functions, vendors, and external organizations. Collaborate with administrative colleagues across the organization, share administrative best practices, and provide or receive backup coverage as needed. Records, Compliance, and Process Management Maintain accurate and organized business records in accordance with company policies and applicable document-retention requirements. Follow established requirements for contracting, procurement, expenses, external engagements, and information handling; identify and escalate potential process or compliance issues appropriately. Use Microsoft 365 and other enterprise platforms to improve organization, communication, document management, and administrative efficiency Knowledge and Skills: Experience supporting multiple senior leaders, preferably at the Vice President level, in a complex and fast-paced organization. Experience in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare, government affairs, public policy, or another highly regulated environment. Experience managing confidential matters and interacting with senior internal and external stakeholders. Experience with procurement, contracting, consultant or vendor administration, invoice workflows, and enterprise systems such as Concur, Coupa, and Icertis, or the ability to learn comparable platforms quickly. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, with strong document-formatting, proofreading, and written communication skills. Demonstrated ability to effectively leverage AI-enabled productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot and other approved enterprise technologies) to improve efficiency, enhance organization, streamline administrative processes, prepare meeting materials, conduct research, and support day-to-day business operations while exercising sound judgment and maintaining compliance with company policies. Proven ability to independently manage multiple projects and a high volume of daily work while maintaining accuracy, follow-through, and attention to detail. Strong judgment and problem-solving skills, including the ability to resolve non-routine issues, communicate conflicts and tradeoffs, and escalate matters appropriately. Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with a highly professional and service-oriented approach. Ability to anticipate needs, adapt quickly to changing priorities, and remain composed and effective under pressure. Excellent organizational skills, initiative, accountability, and motivation. Education and Experience: Typically requires high school or secondary school education Typically requires 2 years of administrative experience, or the equivalent combination of education and experience Pay Range: $39 - $58 Disclosure Statement: The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law. At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations. From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more. Flex Designation: Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible Flex Eligibility Status: In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as: 1. Hybrid : work remotely up to two days per week; or select 2. On-Site : work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility. Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time. #LI-Hybrid Company Information Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation. Vertex is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, or any characteristic protected under applicable law. Vertex is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. Vertex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law. item.description: Legi slative Auditor: TennCare Location: Nashville, Tennessee Join us in our mission to make government work better. Role Snapshot The Legislative Auditor in the Division of Health Provider Review plays an important role in supporting accountability and transparency within TennCare, Tennessee’s Medicaid program. This position performs examinations and desk reviews of participating providers to ensure accuracy, compliance, and the appropriate use of state and federal resources. Why You'll Love This Job • Meaningful work that impacts communities across Tennessee • Flexible schedules and a standard 37.5-hour workweek • Opportunities for professional growth and development • Collaborative and supportive team environment • Comprehensive benefits and work-life balance What You'll Do • Conduct examinations and desk reviews of TennCare provider financial and statistical data to ensure accuracy and compliance. • Analyze cost reports, claims data, and supporting documentation for providers participating in the TennCare program. • Prepare clear, concise, and well-supported working papers that meet auditing standards and best practices. • Assist with development of tools to organize, track, and analyze information. • Perform data analysis to identify trends, inconsistencies, and issues that support audit conclusions and findings. • Communicate results and relevant information clearly to internal leadership, TennCare, and other stakeholders. • Collaborate with team members and support special projects such as rate computation and analysis, provider cost settlements, and reviews of Managed Care Contractors. What We’re Looking For Required: • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with at least 24 semester hours in accounting • Ability to learn quickly, pay close attention to detail, think critically, problem solve, and produce high-quality work • Strong communication skills and ability to work independently and collaboratively • Good judgment and professionalism in interactions with auditees and coworkers Preferred: • Completed coursework or experience in data analytics • Progress toward or interest in obtaining the CPA license (30 semester hours in accounting), which is strongly encouraged for advancement Logistics • Travel: Seasonal travel may be required. Overnight stays are generally limited to Monday–Wednesday evenings based on auditee availability. • Compensation: Competitive salary and benefits, including annual and sick leave, insurance plans, pension, 401(k), college fee waivers, and flexible schedules. item.title: Public Policy Associate
item.description: ABOUT PERPLEXITY Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. More accuracy. More agency. More signal, less noise. Our answer engine handles hundreds of millions of queries every month for people whose questions spark change and whose decisions bend the world toward progress. As our footprint grows, so does the number of policymakers, agencies, and civil society leaders who want to understand what we are building and how we think. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring a Public Policy Associate in Washington, D.C. to sit at the center of Perplexity's engagement with Congress, the executive branch, trade associations, think tanks, and the broader D.C. ecosystem. This work happens where Washington happens, in Hill offices, in coalition meetings across town, and at the occasional evening event where the conversations that matter most actually take place. This is a relationship heavy, execution heavy seat. You've already worked both sides of the table, once inside a congressional office and once representing an organization before Congress, and you know how policy actually moves. Our Comms team and executive leadership set the strategy; you're our boots on the ground who makes it real. You'll build the stakeholder map, carry our message into the rooms that matter, and bring back what policymakers are saying, so that Perplexity shows up early, credibly, and consistently on the policy questions shaping AI. WHAT YOU'LL DO Execute our policy communications strategy set by our Comms and executive leadership teams. Turn company positions into talking points, event backgrounders, and rapid response, and feed intelligence back to our legal, policy, and product teams. Build and hold relationships with Hill staff in personal offices and on committees, executive branch staff, trade associations, think tanks, and civil society organizations. Advocate directly. Take meetings, deliver our positions, and follow bills and rulemakings that affect Perplexity, working within the company's lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements. Run our D.C. event footprint. Hill staff briefings, roundtables, product demos, receptions, dinners, and off sites. Own guest lists, venues, run of show, and follow up. Represent Perplexity in coalitions and trade association working groups. Track what's being said, flag what matters, and bring our point of view into the conversation. Partner with think tanks and civil society groups on convenings, research launches, and joint programming. Prepare our leaders for D.C. engagements. Briefing books, meeting prep, and post meeting recaps that actually get read. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR At least 3 years of professional experience , including time on Capitol Hill in a personal office or on a committee is strongly preferred. External lobbying experience , either at a government relations or law firm representing clients, or in house at a company. Registered lobbying experience under the Lobbying Disclosure Act is strongly preferred. A real Washington network you built yourself, and the instinct to keep growing it. Event execution. You can run a 20 person Hill staff briefing or a 150 person reception end to end without anything slipping. Strong writing. You can turn a meeting into a two paragraph readout and a briefing book into something a principal will actually use. Sound judgment. You know what to escalate, what to handle, and how to represent a company in a room without a script. Genuine curiosity about AI policy and the substance of what Perplexity is building. You don't need to be a technologist, but you do need to want to learn. Comfort with the pace. Mornings, days, and evenings. This is a role for someone energized by the D.C. schedule. Based in Washington, D.C. and in office four days a week, with occasional travel. BONUS Hill experience on judiciary, commerce, intelligence, or AI focused portfolios. Experience staffing a principal at a company, agency, or trade association. Existing relationships across the AI and tech policy community in D.C.

item.title: Vice President Government Affairs
item.description: Over the last 20 years, Ares’ success has been driven by our people and our culture. Today, our team is guided by our core values – Collaborative, Responsible, Entrepreneurial, Self-Aware, Trustworthy – and our purpose to be a catalyst for shared prosperity and a better future. Through our recruitment, career development and employee-focused programming, we are committed to fostering a welcoming and inclusive work environment where high-performance talent of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can build careers within this exciting and growing industry. Job Description Ares Management Corporation is looking to hire a Vice President to join its Government Affairs team. The position will be an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic self-starter to help build and maintain Ares’ Government Affairs function. The Government Affairs function plays a crucial role in advancing the mission and objectives of Ares and our investors by engaging with policymakers across the globe, staying ahead of and responding to legislative and regulatory developments, and driving thought leadership and advocacy. The Vice President of Government Affairs will play a crucial role in building out the Government Affairs function. In this role, the ideal candidate will be responsible for executing on our policy agenda through monitoring policy developments, developing Ares viewpoints, and engaging in advocacy on behalf of the firm. We are looking for a self-directed individual who is a strong written and verbal communicator, is excited to partner with others and can work cross-functionally to execute on aligned priorities. Reporting relationships Reports to: Managing Director, Head of Government Affairs Primary functions and essential responsibilities Specific responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Partner with the Head of Government Affairs in executing the Government Affairs function strategy Monitor and assess impact of policy developments relevant to Ares and the alternative investment management industry Anticipate and assess opportunity, change, and potential risks in the legislative, regulatory, and political realms Shape legislative, regulatory, and administrative policies affecting the alternative investment industry Coordinate, participate in and manage Ares’ membership with trade groups Prepare briefing and presentation materials for engagements with policymakers, regulators, investors and other stakeholders Provide technical recommendations on legislative and regulatory proposals, collaborating closely with other teams to ensure alignment of views across the firm Represent Ares at meetings with government officials or staff, related events, and other relevant forums Collaborate closely with the Communications and Public Investor Relations teams, as well as other internal teams to ensure alignment between government affairs strategies, external communication and Ares’ overall objectives Provide oversight and direction for external government affairs resources, where appropriate From time to time, assist with portfolio company matters involving government stakeholders Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s Degree is required MPA, MPP, MBA, JD, CFA preferred Experience and Skills Required: 8-12 years of relevant experience working in or with legislative, regulatory, or executive branch agencies Prior experience in government affairs for financial services Prior experience writing and contributing to comment letters, drafting legislative language, and developing policy viewpoints for financial services Detailed understanding of and relationships with financial services policymakers Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word General Requirements: Extensive policy, advocacy, and analytical expertise Superior written and verbal communication skills and a demonstrated ability to create content for specified audiences Demonstrated ability to drive consensus among a diverse array of interests and priorities Exceptional client service orientation and ability to collaborate cross functionally Outstanding organizational skills with strong attention to detail Strong time management and prioritization skills Good judgment in terms of escalating issues vs. solving problems independently Comfort in dealing with ambiguity and uncertainty in a dynamic and fast-paced environment Proven ability to learn quickly, display flexibility and adaptability Political awareness, discretion and demonstrated ability to manage sensitive and high impact matters Highest degree of integrity and ethics Reporting Relationships Compensation The anticipated base salary range for this position is listed below. Total compensation may also include a discretionary performance-based bonus. Note, the range takes into account a broad spectrum of qualifications, including, but not limited to, years of relevant work experience, education, and other relevant qualifications specific to the role. $185,000-$250,000 The firm also offers robust Benefits offerings. Ares U.S. Core Benefits include Comprehensive Medical/Rx, Dental and Vision plans; 401(k) program with company match; Flexible Savings Accounts (FSA); Healthcare Savings Accounts (HSA) with company contribution; Basic and Voluntary Life Insurance; Long-Term Disability (LTD) and Short-Term Disability (STD) insurance; Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and Commuter Benefits plan for parking and transit. Ares offers a number of additional benefits including access to a world-class medical advisory team, a mental health app that includes coaching, therapy and psychiatry, a mindfulness and wellbeing app, financial wellness benefit that includes access to a financial advisor, new parent leave, reproductive and adoption assistance, emergency backup care, matching gift program, education sponsorship program, and much more. There is no set deadline to apply for this job opportunity. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the search is no longer active.

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: As a leader in advancing New York’s energy transition, the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) is a credible, objective and trusted partner in energy planning and in deploying new innovative technologies to build an affordable, abundant, reliable, and clean energy system. NYSERDA works with stakeholders statewide, including residents, business owners, developers, community leaders, local government officials, universities, utilities, investors, entrepreneurs, and more, to develop, invest, and foster conditions that: Attract the private sector capital investment needed to expand New York’s clean energy economy. Advance solutions for using clean energy at a large-scale in New York. Enable New York’s communities and residents to benefit equitably in the clean energy transition. Job Overview The Director, Government Affairs reports directly to the VP for Policy Implementation & Intergovernmental Affairs. The Director oversees a Government Affairs (GA) team charged with interfacing with the Executive Chamber, the State Legislature, municipal officials, other state and local agencies and authorities and other key stakeholders to advance NYSERDA’s Mission Outcomes. This work includes crafting and stewarding a proactive strategy to advance Authority priorities, responding to incoming requests from these entities, informing energy and environmental policy discussions that pertain to NYSERDA, developing responses to enacted legislation, and other engagements as needed. Primary Responsibilities Lead NYSERDA engagement with local and state elected officials and staff, including leading development and management of engagement with Legislature and Executive Chamber, support NYSERDA Officers, particularly the CEO, at events, and preparation of background and briefing materials for Senior Executives. Coordinate with Vice President, Policy Implementation & Intergovernmental Affairs and Chief of Staff’s office to develop approach to annual Budget/Legislative Session, including preparation for the President and CEO and Officers at legislative hearings and committee meetings, and ongoing engagement with Chamber and Legislative branches. . In close coordination with NYSERDA Officers and Counsel’s office, manage Legislative Departmental submissions and responses to all legislative inquiries, as well as inform NYSERDA management of legislative developments throughout the State Legislature Session. Prepare and conduct briefings for Executive Team, Officers, and CEO on changes to or opportunities to obtain new critical funding or regulatory actions occurring at federal, state and local levels that would impact the Authority’s ability to advance its responsibilities. Manage and oversee all relations with local and state elected officials and their staff. Oversee constituent services and responses. Coordinate with Communications Team, Events Team, Executive Team and program departments to handle and respond to events, press, etc. Attend and represent NYSERDA at events as needed, including speaking at events, conferences, and functions, as needed. Provide excellent verbal and written products, including ability to craft a compelling business/strategic case for Authority outcomes. Write and edit internal and external communications. Serve as an effective coach and leader providing relevant strategic and management guidance to members of the GA Team as well as other departments. Maintain a robust knowledge of local, state, and Federal key issues, priorities, agenda, and sensitivities, particularly as it relates to climate, clean energy, and electrification. Perform all managerial and supervisory responsibilities with respect, fairness, consistency, and inclusion across the workforce. Other duties assigned to support the Authority’s mission and outcomes. Minimum Qualifications A Bachelor’s degree and 10 years of legislative or relevant experience, including 5 years in supervisory roles In depth knowledge and understanding of legislative processes and actions In-depth understanding of New York State Government and agencies. Genuine passion for advancing sound policy relating to energy and the environment and an interest in developing and supporting a dynamic and talented team. Project management and leadership skills including the ability to work as a team leader and team member, maintain project timelines, budgets, and deliver on commitments. Highest level of communication and interpersonal skills involving the ability to work cross-functionally to understand requirements, present alternatives and recommendations. Self-starter who acts independently, directs one’s own work and can handle diverse tasks quickly and accurately within a high-performance environment. Exceptional manager, coach, mentor, and developer of talent; an ability to lead and develop a team to achieve their potential, innovate and uncover new possibilities, and deliver impactful and relevant outcomes. Demonstrated problem-solving ability, resourcefulness, adaptability, and an instinct for surfacing value and pragmatic solutions. Top-notch presentation and interpersonal skills that resonate with audiences of diverse backgrounds. Relentless work ethic and resolute integrity Strong organizational and analytical skills; ability to quickly aggregate and analyze information. Willingness to occasionally work long or odd hours, especially during Legislative session. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree and 8 years’ experience in legislative and government affairs position including 5 years in supervisory roles. item.title: Political Reporter
item.description: Reporter – New Orleans politics The Times-Picayune has an opening for one of the best beats around: covering the public officials, civic leaders and other bastions of political power in New Orleans. Politics in the Crescent City are dagger sharp and always interesting. We’re looking for an experienced reporter who can navigate the city’s centers of power and the personalities who control them. The goal is to tell great stories about how politics – and the fight for political power – impact the everyday lives of New Orleanians. The city’s passionate politics are an outgrowth of its unique culture, neighborhoods and people. It also has a locally owned, Pulitzer-Prize winning media company that’s served readers for nearly two centuries. The Times-Picayune and our website, NOLA.com, offer distinctive, impactful journalism every day, produced by a team of journalists with decades of experience covering south Louisiana. The company is an equal opportunity employer, committed to recruiting, developing, and promoting a diverse workforce while providing unique opportunities and career paths for our employees. We encourage applicants of all backgrounds and experience levels to apply. This position offers a competitive salary and benefits package that includes medical, vision and dental insurance, short term disability, long term disability and a 401K plan.

item.title: Public Policy Manager
item.description: JOB SUMMARY: The Manager of Public Policy is a member of Truth Initiative's Public Policy team and advances the organization's policy priorities by conducting strategic policy research and analysis; monitoring and evaluating legislative, regulatory, and public health developments related to nicotine and substance use, cannabis, opioids, and other emerging public health issues; developing policy reports, issue briefs; and supporting policy advocacy efforts through research, coalition engagement, and stakeholder education. In addition to contributing to work on nicotine and tobacco issues, The Manager serves as a subject matter expert on substance use and addiction policy issues and works collaboratively across Truth Initiative to translate complex policy developments into actionable insights, evidence-based recommendations, and audience-appropriate materials. DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES (*ESSENTIAL DUTIES): Monitor, research, and analyze federal, state, and local legislation, regulations, and policy developments related to nicotine and tobacco, substance use prevention, cannabis regulation, opioid misuse and overdose prevention, addiction treatment, and related public health issues.* Identify policy trends, emerging issues, and opportunities for organizational engagement, public education, and policy impact.* Produce policy analyses, issue briefs, fact sheets, regulatory summaries, white papers, reports, and other written products.* Draft and support the development of formal comments to federal and state agencies.* Synthesize scientific literature, policy research, surveillance data, and public health evidence into actionable policy recommendations.* Attend and report on hearings, regulatory meetings, policy briefings, and conferences.* Build and maintain relationships with external partners, coalitions, public health organizations, academic institutions, and governmental agencies. Represent Truth Initiative in external meetings, working groups, coalitions, and professional conferences. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Master's degree in Public Policy, Public Health, Health Policy, Political Science, Law, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. 5-7 years of professional experience in public policy, government affairs, health policy, public health advocacy, regulatory affairs, or policy research and analysis. Demonstrated experience in substance use prevention policy, opioid policy, cannabis policy, addiction treatment policy, behavioral health policy, and tobacco control policy. Preferred candidate would have previous exposure to substance use prevention world and contacts Experience monitoring and analyzing legislative and regulatory activity at the federal and/or state levels. Excellent public health policy research and analytical skills. Strong writing, editing, and policy communication skills. Ability to interpret legislation, regulations, scientific evidence, and public health data. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to build productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders. PREFFERED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience working on federal public health, substance use, healthcare, behavioral health, or regulatory policy issues. Familiarity with federal legislative and regulatory processes and agencies including FDA, CDC, SAMHSA, NIH, CMS, DEA, ONDCP, and HHS. Experience drafting or contributing to public comments, Congressional briefings, policy recommendations, or regulatory analyses. Experience engaging with federal agencies, Congressional offices, national advocacy organizations, or public health coalitions. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This position is based in Washington, D.C. with a hybrid work schedule of three days in the office and two telework days. COMPENSATION PACKAGE: The salary range for this role is starting at $85,000-$90,000 per year on a national basis. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to qualifications for the role, relevant work experience, skillset, internal equity, location, and certifications, consistent with applicable law. Salary is just one part of our total rewards package which additionally includes performance bonus for eligible roles, and competitive benefits. Interested candidates should submit their cover letter and resume here OR mail application materials to: Human Resources Attn: Public Policy Manager 900 G Street, NW Fourth Floor Washington, DC 20001 Fax: (202) 204-5214 No telephone calls please. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status or disability.

item.title: Government Affairs Specialist
item.description: The Government Affairs Specialist supports the company's government and regulatory affairs efforts by monitoring and tracking legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments at the international, federal, state, and local levels. Reporting to the Manager of Government Relations, this role coordinates policy updates, prepares monthly reporting materials, supports industry association engagement, and assists in identifying emerging compliance matters, including data privacy regulations. Responsibilities: Monitor and track international legislative and regulatory developments that may impact the business. Assist the Government and Regulatory Affairs team with U.S. legislative, regulatory, and government affairs activities at the federal, state, and local levels. Research, identify, and track regulatory actions and emerging public policy issues. Prepare and distribute monthly government relations updates and reporting materials. Support participation in industry associations and serve as an alternate representative on select committees. Monitor developing data privacy laws and compliance requirements, including CPRA, GDPR, and similar regulations. Summarize policy developments and communicate potential business impacts to internal stakeholders. Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to support the company's government relations objectives. Job Requirements: Associate’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Public Administration, or related experience required. Proven experience in government relations, advocacy, public policy, legislative affairs, or a related field preferred. Understanding of federal, state, and local legislative and regulatory processes. Strong organizational, research, and analytical skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively within a team environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, primarily Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Ability to influence others, maintain confidentiality, and exercise sound judgment. Must be able to work full-time onsite in Middleville, Michigan. This is not a remote position. Middleville, Michigan, United States

item.title: Global Head Of Government Affairs
item.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About You and The Role As Zipline’s Global Head of Government Affairs, you’ll play a critical role in our global success. You’ll design and execute Zipline’s government affairs and public affairs strategy, with the support of the world-class team you build and lead, and you’ll have a direct impact on scaling Zipline's business across the United States, building on our broad footprint in Africa, and launching new markets abroad. Reporting to Zipline’s Chief Legal Officer, this role encompasses public policy, government relations, and public affairs at every jurisdictional level globally. Your key responsibilities will be to: Set our global government affairs and public affairs strategy, tuned to enable Zipline’s rapid growth in the U.S. and abroad. Build and lead a growing team of world-class employees and highly-effective consultants and lobbyists. Drive business-critical outcomes, ranging from landing legislation and regulations that open new international markets, to expanding U.S. regulations governing freedom to operate for commercial drones, to obtaining municipal land use entitlements and permits for Zipline’s ground operations. Create and sustain enduring relationships with electeds and other policymakers at every jurisdictional level, cultivating champions who support Zipline’s mission and business. Build grassroots, grasstops, and third-party advocacy networks, to demonstrate Zipline’s community benefits and support market launches and expansion. Cultivate and mobilize trusted relationships within the communities we serve when the company faces opposition or controversy. Collaborate shoulder-to-shoulder with Zipline's amazing Regulatory Affairs, Legal, and Communications teams to deliver our Government Affairs and Public Affairs strategy. Brief and advise Zipline’s executive team and Board of Directors on global policy risks and opportunities. This role is based in our South San Francisco office and includes significant travel across the U.S. and internationally to engage policymakers and build relationships in the communities we serve. What You'll Do Build and lead Zipline’s global government affairs and public affairs functions, at every jurisdictional level in the U.S. and abroad. Hire, develop, and lead a growing team of world-class professionals and consultants. Own the function’s budget and resourcing decisions. Design, execute, and iterate comprehensive, global government affairs and public affairs strategies that enable Zipline to launch new markets on schedule and scale operations responsibly. Develop and sustain strong, trusted relationships with electeds and other policymakers in every market Zipline serves and plans to serve. Advocate for legislation, regulations, and ordinances that advance Zipline’s business, and lead engagement on rulemaking and policy proposals that affect drone delivery worldwide. Provide critical support for obtaining local land use entitlements and permits for Zipline's infrastructure and operations globally. Support and drive priorities for commercial drone delivery trade associations and other aligned industry groups. Build grassroots, grasstops, coalitions and other third-party advocacy networks to mobilize when the company needs support or faces opposition. Develop and maintain networks of community advocates, including business and civic leaders, former public officials, users and merchants, first responders, academics, faith leaders, healthcare organizations, environmental and road-safety groups, and workforce organizations. Create programs that turn positive community experiences into testimonials, endorsements, data, and stories that demonstrate Zipline’s value and support public advocacy. Work alongside Zipline's Global Head of Regulatory Affairs, who is responsible for aviation legal compliance and regulatory advocacy, and whose team serves as Zipline's subject matter experts in those areas. Work closely with our Legal Team, which is responsible for regulatory interpretation and compliance and government investigations. Collaborate with our Commercial, Customer Experience, Systems Engineering, Marketing, Operations, and Product teams, to drive our business forward. What You'll Bring Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience. 15+ years of progressively senior experience, with prior responsibility for leading a global government affairs function or a substantial regional/global portfolio. Demonstrated experience building and leading high-performing, rapidly growing teams, including hiring, developing, and scaling a global function in a fast-growing organization. Experience successfully onboarding and managing external consultants and lobbyists globally. Excitement for Zipline’s transformational technology and mission, and the ability to communicate our vision and value for communities with authenticity and conviction. Persuasive communicator (verbal and written) who can simplify complex technology, shape public perception, and address common areas of concern with credibility. Creative, first-principles thinker who can build strategy from scratch in an emerging regulatory space rather than relying on existing playbooks. Fast-moving and nimble, able to react quickly to changing circumstances in a dynamic legislative and regulatory environment, and comfortable operating in high-stakes, time-sensitive situations. Established relationships with policymakers, and the ability to build trusted new relationships quickly. Experience leading or working closely with trade associations, coalitions, and industry allies to advance shared policy goals. Ability to translate business goals into strategies that build trust, reduce friction, strengthen Zipline’s reputation, and support rapid growth across diverse communities and political environments. Strong cross-functional leadership skills, with experience partnering collaboratively across an entire organization (including regulatory and legal teams). Ability and willingness to travel globally to engage policymakers and build relationships in the communities we serve. Bonus points for relevant experience working on applicable or analogous technology policy issues (autonomy, robotics, drones, aviation, transportation, or related fields). What Else You Need To Know The starting cash range for this role is $250,000.00-$300,000.00. Please note that this is a target starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash payment for this role will depend on various factors, including a specific candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may include equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental, and vision insurance; paid time off; and more. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

item.description: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes CLEARANCE TYPE: Top Secret TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. The Director of Government Affairs will report directly to the Senior Director, Office of the Secretary of War Customer Relations Team within the Northrop Grumman Corporate Global Business Development organization. Located in Falls Church, VA, the selected candidate will be responsible for expanding and maintaining effective relations between Northrop Grumman and the Department of War, focused on organizations within the Office of the Secretary of War (including Policy, CAPE, and Comptroller) and the Joint Staff. The Director will directly engage with government officials to support Northrop Grumman policy objectives and facilitate engagements for company leaders. Specific responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following: Designing, coordinating, and executing customer engagement plans in support Northrop Grumman policy and program priorities. Providing insights into Department of War policy, personnel, programmatic, budgetary, and legislative initiatives affecting company equities. Orchestrating engagements with organizations within the Office of the Secretary of War with other elements of Northrop Grumman (e.g., Military Service teams) to maximize effectiveness. Effectively representing Northrop Grumman senior leadership views and positions with senior Department of War officials. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 10 years of combined experience in U.S. Government policy and/or defense industry business development or government affairs. Demonstrated experience working with the Department of War, including impactful relationships within the Office of the Secretary of War and Joint Staff. Proven ability to think strategically and integrate policy, political, requirement, and budgetary considerations to inform senior U.S. Government civilian and military decision makers. Knowledgeable of Department of War processes, including PPBE and Acquisition, and familiarity with ongoing policy reforms. Excellent organizational, verbal, and written communication skills, as well as project management, analytical, planning, and presentation skills. Active Top Secret security clearance with the ability to obtain the SCI; maintaining the required security clearance will be a condition of continued employment. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in National Security or related discipline and/or a minimum of 15 years of combined experience in U.S. Government policy and/or defense industry business development or government affairs Executive presence to include a high level of judgement, initiative, integrity, and hands-on approach to problem solving both internal and external to the company. A team player, self-starter, with a strong work ethic and ability to work cooperatively across the organization without significant support. Primary Level Salary Range: $203,900.00 - $305,900.00 The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. item.description: Our Company Changing the world through digital experiences is what Adobe’s all about. We give everyone—from emerging artists to global brands—everything they need to design and deliver exceptional digital experiences. We’re passionate about empowering people to craft beautiful and powerful images, videos, and apps, and transform how companies interact with customers across every screen. Our goal is to recruit top talent, and we are committed to building outstanding employee experiences where everyone is respected and has access to equal opportunity. We realize that new ideas can arise from everywhere in the organization, and we know the next big idea could be yours! The Opportunity The Adobe Government Relations and Public Affairs team seeks an innovative and well-connected federal government relations professional. The role offers a dynamic and enjoyable work environment. If you enjoy helping others achieve their goals, building an extensive network of relationships inside the U.S. legislative branch, advocating for a cause, and building consensus with other like-minded organizations, this position may be for you. A successful candidate will have knowledge of technology policy, federal appropriations, and federal agency IT budgeting and modernization processes. This role requires excellent communication and writing ability, high energy, and a curiosity about the constantly evolving technology policy, artificial intelligence, and the government IT modernization space. The position reports to the Director of U.S. Federal Government Relations (U.S. Legislative Branch) in Adobe’s Washington, DC office. What you'll Do Serve as a key liaison between Adobe business leadership and U.S. congressional offices (House & Senate), driving impactful policy and business engagements. Advocate for innovative technology policy solutions across the U.S. Legislative Branch in areas such as artificial intelligence, creators’ rights, consumer protection, and federal IT modernization. Partner with US federal executive branch government relations team to assist in developing and advancing government relations advocacy objectives and public policy priorities. Coordinate with the U.S. public sector sales team to promote essential US federal agency business aims. Aid in advancing federal budget and appropriations initiatives. Assist in coordinating and managing all components of the Public Sector Advisory Board. Attend congressional hearings, government-industry events, and trade association meetings and report back to the business; Build and manage advocacy efforts through active engagement with Congress, trade associations, consultants, and industry peers. Assist in advocating for federal procurement and digital government policies that improve the customer experience and the digital service delivery provided by government. What you need to succeed 5 -10 years of proven experience. Experience working with or within the U.S. executive and legislative branches of government. Experience with technology and artificial intelligence policy and the federal appropriations process. Excellent interpersonal skills – both written and oral. Proficient in using artificial intelligence tools and MS PowerPoint to develop presentations and strategy documents for public affairs. Skilled at employing MS Excel, Word, and Adobe Acrobat to manage team tasks and write policy papers. Interest in evangelizing responsible AI, content authenticity, and federal digital government policy issues. Ability to think and act both strategically and creatively. Strong program and project management skills to leverage in managing the advisory board for the government sector business. Strong self-starter who is a phenomenal teammate and excels developing and completing their own work plan. Ability to take complicated technical concepts and translate in a compelling and succinct manner on paper and in-person. Knowledge of federal government agencies’ structure and functions. Must be willing to register as a Federal Lobbyist. Bachelor’s degree required. Passionate about government service and the role of government in society. Strong desire for success At Adobe, you will be immersed in an exceptional work environment that is recognized throughout the world on Best Companies lists. You will also be surrounded by colleagues who are committed to helping each other grow through our unique Check-In approach where ongoing feedback flows freely. If you’re looking to make an impact, Adobe's the place for you. Discover what our employees are saying about their career experiences on the Adobe Life blog and explore the meaningful benefits we offer. Adobe is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and encourage diversity in the workplace regardless of gender, race or color, cultural background or country of origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. About Adobe Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity. Our 30,000+ employees worldwide are creating the future and raising the bar as we drive the next decade of growth. We’re on a mission to hire the very best and believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. At Adobe, we believe that great ideas can come from anywhere in the organization. The next big idea could be yours. Let’s Adobe together At Adobe, we believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. Learn more about Adobe life, including our values and culture , focus on people, purpose and community , Adobe for All , comprehensive benefits programs , the stories we tell , the customers we serve, and how you can help us advance our mission of empowering everyone to create. Adobe is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Learn more. Adobe aims to make our Careers website and recruiting process accessible to any and all users. item.description: Job Closes: 09/13/2026 GENERAL SUMMARY Develops and implements intergovernmental and public information programs, events, and materials designed to promote and advance the mission and goals of the San Antonio River Authority. Primary responsibility will be representing the San Antonio River Authority with elected officials and residents in Wilson, Karnes, and Goliad counties. Safety is #1 at the River Authority: We expect every employee: to 1) Strictly follow safety policies, rules, and safe work methods. 2) Promptly correct or report safety hazards or unsafe conditions. Immediately report injuries for prompt diagnosis and treatment. 3) Make regular suggestions for safety process improvements to support continuous safety improvement. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by employees in this job. Employees may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description. Develops and implements intergovernmental and public information projects from inception to completion; meeting project requirements, deadlines, budget, and quality standards. Supports the planning, project development, project operation elements, and strategic initiatives related to the River Authority’s mission. Establishes relationships with elected officials and their staff, public agency staff, chambers of commerce and other San Antonio River Basin civic groups to convey River Authority projects, vision and mission. Initiates, develops, implements, and staffs intergovernmental and community meetings and events including local, regional, and state legislative committee hearings and meetings, public meetings and events, luncheons, and field trips. Manages stakeholder processes for major projects of the River Authority, including public input meetings and stakeholder committees. Coordinates interactions with stakeholders, cross functional teams, and senior leaders. Assists in the development of the federal, state and local legislative agendas. Tracks progress of legislative and congressional strategies for the River Authority and reports updates to the Board, Executive Team and Managers. Reviews and analyzes regulations, legislation, laws, and public policy for updates. Creates public information materials for the River Authority including brochures, newsletters, news releases, media advisories, speaking/copy points, presentations, and other necessary materials. Supports social media activities across multiple platforms. Develops and oversees distribution of a variety of informational materials to special interest groups. Serves as a department liaison for one or more internal departments. Serves as the Public Information Act (PIA) officer as delegated; tracks and maintains related documents, and attends required PIA training in accordance with Texas Government Code section 552.012. Delivers River Authority (Speakers Bureau) presentations throughout the district. Performs related work as required. SUPERVISIOR REQUIREMENT This position does not directly supervise any employees. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Required Education and Experience A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Political Science, Public Administration, Public Policy, Communications or a related discipline, and two (2) years’ of progressively responsible experience in intergovernmental, elected officials or in government affairs for an interest group; or a combination of experience and education that results in the required knowledge, skills, and abilities. Required Licenses or Certifications ☒ Must have and maintain a valid driver’s license and an insurable driving record. COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESSFUL PERFORMANCE OF JOB DUTIES The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills and abilities required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Knowledge of: The organization’s mission and vision Microsoft Office Suite Website research and social media techniques Skills and Abilities: Oral and written communication; executing work per organizational bylaws and guiding documents Technical writing and report preparation Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships Must be able to function in a principle-based organization that has a culture that reflects our Values In Action of Accountability, Excellence, Open and Direct Communication, Teamwork and Collaboration. item.title: Director State Government Affairs Southeast Us
item.description: The Opportunity: Reporting to the Senior Director, State Government Affairs, as the Director of State Government Affairs, Southeast US you will be the key point of contact for government officials and stakeholders on state legislative and government policy matters that affect CSL Behring in the Southeast US region. You will have a proven ability to prioritize state activity and a demonstrated understanding of how government actions affect our patients and company operations. You will represent CSL and its facilities in the Southeast US region regarding public policy concerns and is responsible for state legislative and state regulatory policy interactions. You will collaborate with internal departments—such as market access, government reporting,reimbursement, corporate accounts, communications, marketing, sales, and our CSL Plasma business unit—will be essential, and the Director will be responsible for leading team efforts to assess and address policy issues impacting access to care and business operations in the assigned region. You will serve as the company liaison on policy matters with state patient advocacy organizations, trade associations, state medical societies and other groups with complementary policy goals. You will need to be based in the Southeast US region – TX, OK, AR, LA, MS, AL, KY, WV, VA, NC, SC, GA, FL. The Role: Represent CSL Behring and serve as key point of contact for public officials in the assignedregion, developing and maintaining relationships with members of state legislatures, committeestaff, administrative and regulatory officials, and identifying legislative and administrativechampions to advocate on issues affecting CSL Behring. Represent CSL Behring before variousstate legislative committees, agencies, etc. with regard to CSLB priorities. Provide legislative strategy and regulatory analysis in addition to political analysis and strategy.Draft legislation, provide technical corrections, and develop support for priorities. Must be ableto provide clear, relevant and succinct analysis and guidance to CSLB leadership and cross-functional teams. Represents our site operations throughout the Southeast region. Support the growth of CSL Plasma by identifying and developing public official champions andadvancing strong public policy that supports plasma donation. Assess and address legislativeand state regulatory issues affecting the CSL Plasma network. Support CSL’s product portfolio by creating and implementing action plans to advance statelegislative and regulatory initiatives that allow for access to CSLB therapies. Specifically,advocate for Medicaid policies to ensure patient access to CSL Behring therapies. Collaborationwith internal teams is essential, including market access, corporate accounts, reimbursement,contracting, communications, and others. Ability to lead cross-functional discussions, developand implement action plans, build grass roots support, and communicate status updates andresults to diverse stakeholders. Develop and execute relationship strategies for allies and patient advocacy organizations toadvance advocacy initiatives. Build and maintain grassroots coalitions, serving as key point ofcontact for policy and advocacy. Coordinate with other CSLB departments with responsibilitiesrelated to patient group outreach, and work with Policy, Advocacy, and Government Affairsteam on positioning CSL Behring’s state advocacy efforts, determining strategies and tactics inassigned states that support CSL Behring’s commitment to state advocacy. Prepare written summaries of legislation, government action, and analysis of issues for a rangeof audiences, including corporate leadership, patient advocacy organizations, and otherstakeholders. Develop concise and insightful presentations for patient advocacy organizationsand contribute articles as needed to corporate publications and communication channels.Ability to express major points in writing while translating complex topics into lay language isessential. Represent CSL Behring and participate in state affairs committees for trade associations whereCSL Behring has membership (PhRMA, BIO, state Biotech Associations, Chambers, etc.) Work and contribute as a team player by sharing best practices, communicating relevantinsights on issues and intelligence, leading special projects, and coordinating with teammembers to ensure CSL Behring State Government Affairs coverage of key meetings, events,and activities. Manage the business relationship and direct key activities of contract consultants in designatedstates and/or projects in order to advance our policy objectives. Your Skills & Abilities: Bachelor’s degree required (advanced degree preferred) in public policy, government, political science, or related field. 7+ years’ experience preferred, with demonstrated knowledge of the legislative and regulatory process, particularly in the Southeast US region. Previous experience in government affairs or state government is necessary, with state legislative experience desirable. Previous advocacy experience with pharmaceutical/biotech, trade associations or patient advocacy organizations is also highly desirable. Business acumen: understands the life sciences industry and how current and potential policies,trends and practices could affect the industry. Customer focus: able to establish and maintain effective relationships with internal and externalcustomers and gain their trust and respect. Timely decision-making: can make decisions in a timely manner, sometimes with incompleteinformation and under tight deadlines and pressure. Negotiation skills: Can negotiate skillfully in tough situations with both internal and externalgroups. Political Savvy. Priority setting and strong time management. Able to be a self-starter. Strong written communication and presentation skills. About CSL Behring CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives. CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries. To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/ . Our Benefits For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL . You Belong at CSL At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future. To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging Equal Opportunity Employer CSL is an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you are an individual with a disability and need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, please visit https://www.csl.com/accessibility-statement .
